== Biography ==
Adam Glasgow is associated with the family of [[Glasgow-1675|William Glasgow]] and [[Glendinning-340|Nancy Glendinning]] of Killycurragh, County Tyrone. He has been reported as born about 1840, while another birth estimate is 1834; neither date is established by the family memorial. The family account records his death in 1907 and burial at Dayton, Montgomery County, Ohio. These life details require reconciliation with another Adam Glasgow rather than being used to merge the men.

=== The named Glendinning-family son ===
The 1903 Glendinning memorial names Adam among William and Nancy’s five sons, with [[Glasgow-3148|Henry Cunningham]], [[Glasgow-3149|Isaac Watts]], [[Glasgow-3150|Benjamin]] and [[Glasgow-2825|Alexander Flemming]], and names daughters [[Glasgow-3158|Mary]], [[Glasgow-3146|Matilda]] and [[Glasgow-3147|Jane]]. It describes William as a farmer and businessman of Killycorragh. Nancy, whose mother was Mary Bell, was described as the fifth daughter, born in April 1803; the book records her death at Belle Center on 20 March 1890, with reported age 87.<ref name="GlendinningMemorial1903">''A Brief Memorial of the Deceased Members of the Glendinning Family, from the Siege of Derry to the Present Time'' (1903), [https://glendinning.name/history/irish_glendinning.pdf#page=17 PDF p.17], without a printed page number; cover and page visually verified 24 October 2026. Retrospective family publication.</ref>

The book gives no birth date, marriage, death or identifying later occupation for Adam. Its discussion of sons’ railway service and the Nickleplate line does not identify which sons undertook that service. The order of the five sons followed by three daughters does not establish their full birth order or support an estimated birthday.<ref name="GlendinningMemorial1903" />

== Research Notes ==
=== Adult identity and father assessment ===
William remains the selected father at '''77% probable'''. The memorial explicitly names a son Adam in the household; identifying that child with this later adult is a separate inference. The inherited tree account names William and Nancy and gives an Irish origin, but the 1834/1840 birth conflict and the comparison with [[Glasgow-2387|Adam Glasgow (1841–1907)]], Ohio-born son of Arthur, remain unresolved. A matching name and death year do not establish one man. No merger, maternal assessment or vital correction is inferred.

The 22 October 2026 father review was based on the held FamilySearch tree citation and associated narrative. The inspected memorial now supplies the named child role, while the complete adult-to-parent profile proposition remains 77%. William’s own father remains unknown; the book supplies no older Glasgow parent or kinship clause.

Useful discriminating sources are Adam’s Cleveland death record and military-home admissions, compared for parents, age, birthplace and family contacts against Adam-2387’s Arthur household. The memorial and tree should not substitute for that comparison.
